chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The lost property (luqata) is of two types: the lost property of the Sanctuary (Al-Haram) is publicized for a year; if you find its owner, [return it], otherwise give it in charity; and the lost property of elsewhere is publicized for a year; if its owner comes, [return it], otherwise it becomes like part of your wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for keeping or giving away lost property in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the specific fiqh of *luqata* by distinguishing between the Sacred Sanctuary (*Al-Haram*) and other regions, noting that unclaimed items in the Haram are given in charity (*sadaqah*) after a year, whereas elsewhere they become the finder's property (*kasab Malik*). This distinction highlights the unique sanctity and administrative jurisdiction of the Haram, reflecting the practical legal adaptations of the Shia school regarding public rights and ownership acquisition. The ruling underscores the balance between preserving the owner's right and preventing the hoarding of lost goods in sacred spaces.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The findings are of two (types of) findings. A finding of the Al-Harram would be publicised for a year. So if its owner is found, or else it should be given in charity with it; and a finding somewhere else would be publicised for a year. So if its owner comes up, or else it would be like part of your wealth’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar who has said

the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’Findings are of two kinds. The findings, in al-Haram (the sacred area), are publicized for one year. If the owner is found, it is delivered to him; otherwise, it is given in charity. The findings, in non-al-Haram (the sacred area), are publicized for one year. If the owner comes it is his; otherwise, it is like one’s own belongings.’”
